Research snapshot: 21 October 2026

Public BPSC materials and online retailer listings were checked. The research inventory records 3 official source documents and 16 book / question-bank / preparation-set listings. It does not claim every physical-market title has been found or that full book text has been acquired.
Primary audience: General BCS candidates and Special BCS Health candidates.
Main product differentiator: adaptive study plans and evidence-based weakness analysis.
Build approach: AI coding tool with a real backend, verified content, and server-side scoring.
Core principle: one learning engine, separate exam configurations, one verified source of truth.
1. Executive decision

Build BCS Crack as a study-planning and question-practice system, not merely a question repository. The platform should diagnose knowledge, schedule study, deliver exam-accurate practice, analyze errors, and adapt the next plan using real attempt data.
Research finding that changes the product model

The official 51st Special BCS syllabus separates shared subjects from Medical Science and Dental Science professional sections. Inside Special Health, the user must select an intended post: Assistant Surgeon or Assistant Dental Surgeon. These professional banks must not be blended.
The first complete learning loop
1. Candidate selects an exam track and, for Special Health, the professional stream.
2. Candidate states available study time and completes a diagnostic test.
3. System maps responses to syllabus topics and calculates a baseline.
4. Planner generates daily tasks and revision sessions within the candidate’s time budget.
5. Candidate takes topic quizzes or a full mock test under the correct scoring configuration.
6. Weakness analysis updates topic priorities and explains what changes in the next plan.
What research does and does not establish
Verified: BPSC has an official circular, a 30-page Special BCS syllabus published on 30 September 2026, and Form-1 / SMS / admit-card instructions published on 1 October 2026.
Verified from listings: multiple publishers have issued 51st Special BCS Health guides, Medical Science MCQ banks, historical question solutions, and a dedicated Dental Science Parts 1–2 book.

Not yet done: full physical-book inspection, authoritative answer validation of every listed question, publisher licence negotiation, and a claim that this online inventory includes every available title.

4. Content strategy: from books to a verified question bank

The books are candidate sources, not the product database. The application needs its own normalized, reviewed content layer linked back to the underlying source. Store the origin of every imported or newly authored question and keep copyrighted source text separate from original app material.
Source priority
1. Tier 1 — BPSC circular, the official 30-page syllabus, official application notices, and official amendments.
2. Tier 2 — legally acquired Special Health books, used for syllabus mapping and historical-question indexing under a rights policy.
3. Tier 3 — previous Special BCS/medical recruitment questions with established provenance and answer review.
4. Tier 4 — expert-written original practice questions mapped to the official syllabus.
5. Tier 5 — AI-generated practice in a visibly unverified pool until qualified review and source checks are complete.

Field
Reason

Editorial QA workflow
1. Acquire official source / licensed copy and register edition, ISBN if available, publisher, date, and permitted uses.
2. Extract only the necessary question metadata and source references allowed by the rights agreement.
3. Map each item to the current official syllabus topic and professional stream.
4. Check answer key against authoritative reference(s); high-impact medical/dental items require a qualified reviewer.
5. Flag disputes and duplicates instead of averaging conflicting answer keys automatically.
6. Publish only approved items in verified banks; keep drafts and AI-generated items out of verified mock exams.

Rule update and content publication
1. Exam manager registers the source notice and creates a draft configuration version.
2. Rules are checked for completeness and mark totals; second reviewer approves the draft.
3. Published configuration applies to new test sessions; previous attempts retain their original snapshots.
4. Question editor drafts/imports a question, assigns source and syllabus topic, and submits it for review.
5. Reviewer confirms answer/explanation and rights status. Only approved questions enter verified banks.
8. AI-personalized study and weakness engine
Inputs
Exam configuration and official topic hierarchy.
Candidate’s daily minutes, study days, deadline/planning horizon and language preference.
Diagnostic and test attempts, answer correctness, unanswered items, time per question, revision outcomes and task completion history.
Weakness labels
Likely issue
Evidence
Action
Knowledge gap
Repeated incorrect responses in a topic
Review fundamentals and practise easier items, then retest.
Retention problem
Topic was previously known but delayed revision fails
Schedule spaced revision and mixed retrieval practice.
Careless error
Known topics still fail through misreading or option selection
Short careful-reading drills and explanation of trap patterns.
Time pressure
Accuracy falls in timed work or time per item is high
Short timed sets and pacing practice.
Guessing risk
Low-confidence responses tend to be wrong, when confidence data exists
Review concept and option-elimination methods.
Unassessed topic
Insufficient response history
Schedule a diagnostic or first-learning task, not a weak-topic verdict.
Planner behavior
1. Create strategic, weekly and daily plans. Every task has a topic, duration, completion condition and reason.
2. Validate the sum of daily minutes against user availability. Enforce exam track and prerequisite constraints.
3. After an attempt, update topic metrics and reschedule revision. Modify upcoming tasks instead of rebuilding the plan arbitrarily.
4. If the candidate misses several days, offer a feasible recovery plan rather than a growing impossible backlog.

5. A readiness indicator may combine recent accuracy, syllabus coverage, retention and timed-test performance. Label it as an internal preparation heuristic, show its components and do not present it as selection probability.

Controls that must exist before public launch
Server-side authorization and PostgreSQL row-level security; hiding an admin button is not authorization.
Server-controlled test start/expiry/submission; validate answers, calculate marks on server, and prevent duplicate submissions.
Rate limits and usage ceilings for auth, question endpoints and AI service calls.
Strict schema validation of model outputs; no direct SQL or privileged actions from model-generated text.
Separate staging/production environments, secret management, backups and restoration test.
Content issue-reporting, account deletion/export workflow, privacy policy and minimal personal-data collection.
Audit records for rule changes, answer corrections, role changes, publication and user suspension.

Limitations and next research actions
Retail listings may be updated, discounted, out of stock, or duplicate the same title across merchants; price and stock are snapshots only.
Several pages give incomplete author, page-count, syllabus coverage or table-of-contents details. Inspect a lawful sample/physical copy before mapping.

Before using book-derived text or questions in production, obtain clear rights covering digitization, OCR, search, embeddings/RAG, excerpts and display. A retail purchase is not necessarily a digital redistribution licence.
Have subject experts verify Medical Science and Dental Science answers; never allow the LLM alone to certify them.
